title: Introduce operator audit enricher and KMS origin boundaries
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Several customers requested tighter provenance and operator context in audit logs to meet regulatory requirements for key usage and operator activity. Current audit events include service and tenant identifiers but lack an authoritative operator provenance and KMS origin mapping. This PR introduces an "operator audit enricher" middleware that augments outgoing audit events with operator-scoped assertions, KMS key origin tags, and a compact residency vector. It also wires a lightweight OPA evaluation hook that rejects requests where an operator's region-bound policy conflicts with the requested KMS origin. The changes are focused, backward-compatible, and feature-flagged for a staged rollout. Key changes: 1) audit/enricher: new middleware that attaches operator_claims (operator_id, operator_role, auth_method), kms_origin_hint (provider, region, key_meta_hash), and residency_vector (geo_zone, jurisdiction_flags) to every audit event emitted from the control plane; 2) kms/origin-mapper: mapping table and runtime validator that resolves request KMS key IDs to authoritative origin metadata and emits a KMS provenance token used by downstream services; 3) opa/policy-hook: an inline OPA evaluation point in the authz pipeline that consults a residency-aware policy bundle to allow/deny operator->key operations; 4) observability: new metrics (audit.enriched.count, audit.enricher.latency_ms, kms.origin.mismatches) and a Grafana dashboard draft; 5) migration/rollout: feature flag (feature.operator_audit_enricher) and a canary rollout plan targeting 5% of traffic for 72 hours with telemetry gates (no increase in audit error rate, <1% kms.origin.mismatches); 6) tests: unit tests for enrichment logic, integration tests covering OPA policies, and an end-to-end smoke that validates enrichment round-trip to the audit sink. Backwards compatibility and safety: enrichment runs after authentication and before audit dispatch. If origin mapping fails or OPA is unreachable, behavior is controlled by the feature flag and a configured failure_mode (fail_open | fail_closed). Default for this rollout is fail_open with a metric alarm. Files added/modified are limited to the audit, authz, kms, and observability packages to minimize blast radius. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked: Linear ENG-2129 - [x] Unit and integration tests added - [x] Feature flag gating and rollout plan included - [x] Observability and alerting updates - [x] Ops migration notes and CLI tooling for retroactive enrichment (see migration/README) Reference: related PRs for residency enforcement and KMS origin proofing (see linked Linear items).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Please ensure the KMS origin mapping is cached with TTL to avoid extra KMS metadata lookups on the hot path.
Maya Chen: Implemented an in-memory LRU cache with configurable TTL; added metrics for cache_hit_ratio and a cache warm-up in canary.
Priya Reddy: OPA evaluation may add latency; can we short-circuit for operators with a tenant-scoped allowlist?
Maya Chen: Added an allowlist fast-path in authz that checks operator_scope first and skips OPA if matched; documented caveat in migration notes.
Diego Alvarez: Integration test failed once on CI with a transient OPA timeout, suggest increasing test timeouts and marking as flaky if necessary.
Maya Chen: Increased retry/backoff around OPA in tests and added a retry-on-flaky label for the integration job. CI flakiness root cause appears to be test infra CPU contention.
ci_checks: integration-tests: fail on first run (OPA timeout), rerun: pass
merge_outcome: Merged via squash merge after 2 approvals. No blocking CI failures. Release note entry added and canary started immediately post-merge.
release_notes: Adds an operator audit enrichment pipeline that embeds operator claims and KMS origin metadata in audit events. Adds an OPA residency check to prevent operator->key operations that violate region policies (feature-flagged). Metrics and dashboards included. Rollout: staged canary, default fail_open. Admins can retroactively enrich historical audit batches using opsctl migrate-enrichments.
migration_instructions: 1) Enable feature.operator_audit_enricher=false in staging cluster. 2) Run opsctl migrate-enrichments --dry-run against a representative audit shard to validate enrichment tokens. 3) Flip feature flag to true for 5% canary using the console. 4) Monitor audit.enricher.latency_ms and kms.origin.mismatches; if thresholds exceeded, rollback canary. 5) After 72h and no regressions, increment canary to 25% then 100%.
notes_for_ops: Tooling: opsctl now includes a migrate-enrichments subcommand that can retroactively attach provenance tokens to stored audit batches; recommended to run in read-only dry-run first. Alert: create an alert on kms.origin.mismatches > 1% sustained for 5m. Default failure_mode in config is 'fail_open' to reduce impact.
security_review_summary: Security reviewed by SecEng; concerns around KMS key metadata confidentiality were addressed by storing only cryptographic hash of key meta (key_meta_hash) in audit payloads and by encrypting the provenance token with the cluster KMS. RBAC changes are additive and scoped to operator claims; no privilege escalation paths detected.
post_merge_tasks: - Monitor canary metrics for 72h - Publish ops migration guide to internal runbook - Coordinate with Customer Success for tenants in high-regulatory jurisdictions - Create follow-up ticket ENG-2180 for opt-in enforced fail_closed behavior after telemetry baseline established
